messages:
maya: Heads-up — I'm prototyping a per-tier canary that is region-aware and composes model-variant fallbacks. Trying to capture what the API should expose and how Console should show exposure + fallback mapping.

jon: mmk. what are the hard constraints? latency vs cost vs isolation?

maya: primary constraints: 1) gold customers get low-latency routing (no quantized fallbacks unless explicit), 2) silver/beta can get cheaper variants, 3) regional capacity may trigger fallback to compatible variants in other regions or lower-Q models.

dmitri: sounds like we need routing policy that is a composition of rules: tier -> region -> model-pool -> fallback-chain. can we express that in existing policy proto?

maya: current proto is pretty flat. thinking of adding "scopes" and "composition" so a single route can declare per-scope exposure. example sketch: 

```json
{
  "route": "/v1/generate",
  "scopes": {
    "tier:gold": { "variants": ["gptx-1.0"], "exposure": 0.05 },
    "tier:silver": { "variants": ["gptx-1.0","gptx-quant"], "exposure": 0.2 },
    "region:eu": { "fallthrough": "region:na" }
  },
  "fallback": ["gptx-quant","gpt-small-8bit"]
}
```

maya: This lets us scope canary exposure per-tier and per-region, then apply a global fallback chain if the scoped variants fail capacity checks.

amy: UI question: how does Console show effective routing for a customer? e.g., if a request comes from eu + silver, which variant wins? we need a single-line summary + expanded decision tree.

jon: Agreed. summary: "silver/eu -> 10% gptx-1.0 (canary) else gptx-quant (fallback)". Expanded: show the scopes checked in order and telemetry links for each decision.

fern-sre: For telemetry: we need token-level cost + latency broken down by variant+region+tier. Also an alert when fallback rate > X% for a route.

maya: good call. want default alert at 5% fallback for gold routes, 15% for silver.

dmitri: dep questions: How do we compute exposure deterministically across rollout and routing? We should reuse our existing sampling RNG seeded by customer id + route to keep sticky assignment.

maya: yep — sticky assignment is required for canaries. but what about fallback that crosses region? if we route to another region for capacity, sticky assignment must be preserved per-customer.

jon: implementation: routing-layer returns an ordered candidate list to serving runtime, runtime tries in order with quotas/entitlements checked. If first candidate fails (no capacity), runtime falls back to next. We need an API change: route.lookup(...) -> [candidates], plus reason codes in logs.

dmitri: reason codes please. short codes: NO_CAP, QUOTA_EXCEEDED, REGION_UNREACHABLE, ABED (ab test mismatch).

maya: +1. Also we should emit an event: routing.decision with fields: route, customer_tier, region, chosen_variant, fallback_chain_used (list), reason_codes (list). this will feed Console and alerts.

amy: Console UX: show the last 24h routing.decision histogram and a sample trace of decision steps for a single request. add a "simulate" button where you select tier+region+seed to see expected candidate list.

fern-sre: ops note: make sure fallback across regions respects data residency flags. gold customers may forbid cross-region. add a flag in scope: "cross_region_allowed": true/false.

maya: yes — default false for private deployments. public cloud default true.

deploy-bot: deploy started: routing-service v2.14.0 -> canary(10%) (sha: ab12cd3) :rocket:

jon: whoops — try not to merge the proto until runtime and console hooks exist. canary will only affect hosted until we add private config.

maya: noted — I'll gate the proto behind feature-flag and add Console skeleton before we widen.

amy: action items: maya to PR proto + sample Console wireframe; dmitri to add reason codes + sampling logic; jon to draft runtime candidate-list API; fern-sre to add alerts/residency checks.

maya: thanks. tagging @dmitri @jon for visibility :eyes: — if no objections I'll start the proto PR tomorrow.

dmitri: no objections from me. :+1:

jon: go for it.

fern-sre: ack.
thread_summary: Per-tier & region-aware canary routing design discussion: proto sketch, runtime candidate-list API, Console UX for decision tracing, telemetry & alerts, residency constraints.
